summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on sizing reserved GPU pool and burst/fallback strategies. Customer wants predictable p99 < 300ms for short chat requests at typical concurrency 40-80, burstable to 250 concurrent with graceful fallback to smaller model. Agreement on a short benchmark followed by a 4-week pilot on reserved capacity if results meet success criteria.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luca (Redwood Solutions), Marcus (Avalon CTO), Tanya (Avalon SRE), Priya S. (Avalon ML), Ethan (Avalon PM)
---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda is sizing and the POC plan for capacity and burst. can we go around real quick?
[00:12] Marcus: sure, Marcus Lee. main thing for us is predictable latency under typical load, and how reserved vs burst works, cost math.
[00:22] Tanya: Tanya Ruiz, SRE. i care about autopilot scaling behaviors and fallback so we don't blow up our VPC peering.
[00:30] Jordan: great, Priya SE will walk through the runtime and recommended config.
[00:36] Priya (SE): hi everyone. one high level: for POC we usually propose a small reserved pool sized to handle base concurrency and a burst buffer for ~3x headroom. the buffer can be dedicated GPUs or shared burst from the cloud. question for you - what's your baseline concurrency and request size?
[00:55] Priya S (ML): our chat RPS is low but concurrency peaks ~50 during morning batch, token per request avg ~180 tokens, max 1.2k. latency sensitivity: p95 < 200ms for short prompts, p99 ideally < 350ms.
[01:15] Priya (SE): okay that maps. if we assume model is a ~20B open model quantized to int8, throughput per GPU for short requests is ~140-180 requests/min depending on kernel. so for steady concurrency 40-60 we'd recommend 2 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs plus a burst pool of 2 additional gpus for spikes.
[01:42] Marcus: can you translate that to cost? also is fallback to a smaller model automated?
[01:50] Jordan: yes cost sheet will show reserved commit vs on-demand burst. fallback - we support policy-based routing: route to cheaper model variant or fallback region when latency SLO is at risk. SE: can you explain warm KV cache effect?
[02:05] Priya (SE): sure - prefix/KV caching reduces compute for repeated session tokens; in chat where users have continuations, cache hit can reduce p99 by ~25-40%. warming matters for short POC windows. we'll include warm-up steps in the benchmark. note: transcription sometimes shows KV as K V cash, we see that on other calls too.
[02:28] Tanya: what about cold starts when burst spins up? we worry about initial latency spike.
[02:34] Priya (SE): good point. bursting can be provisioned as fast-boot containers or pre-warmed GPUs. two patterns: cold burst (cheaper, 30-90s spin) or kept-warm burst (higher cost, <10s spin). for your SLA I'd recommend kept-warm burst pool of 1-2 GPUs and an autoscaler policy that starts an additional 1 on demand with fallback routing.
[03:00] Marcus: fallback routing meaning send to smaller model or queue requests?
[03:05] Priya (SE): both options. typical enterprise approach: primary model -> if p99 breaches, route subsequent requests to an L7 fallback model (eg 7B quantized) or apply partial responses + client-side retry. Redwood can do automatic percent rollouts or fixed thresholds.
[03:22] Ethan: what metrics do we need to accept POC?
[03:25] Jordan: success criteria we propose: 1) p95 < 250ms and p99 < 350ms for typical short prompts at baseline concurrency for 48-hour run; 2) graceful degradation under 3x baseline with functional responses from fallback model; 3) memory/throughput numbers and cost per 1M tokens within agreed band.
[03:45] Marcus: that seems fair. timeline?
[03:48] Jordan: recommended timeline: share pricing and config by Monday (Jordan), run benchmarks week of Aug 27 for 48 hours (Priya) using your traffic trace, analyze results and decide on a 4-week reserved pilot starting ~Sep 8.
[04:06] Priya (SE): i'm going to outline the exact load profile - concurrency ramps, spike shapes (sine vs saw) and synthetic vs replayed traces. replay gives more realistic cache behavior.
[04:20] Tanya: we'll share an anonymized 7-day CDN trace, stripped of PII. could you confirm what headers/annotations you need?
[04:28] Priya (SE): send CSV with timestamp, latency, tokens requested, user session id. session id helps with prefix cache sim.
[04:36] Marcus: any security blockers? we need SOC2 + SSO and KMS support.
[04:41] Jordan: Redwood supports SOC2 and KMS integrations; Private/VPC option available for pilot if required. we'll attach our security pack and SOC2 report.
[04:50] Marcus: good. one more on autoscaling: how do you prevent noisy neighbor in shared burst?
[04:55] Priya (SE): policy: we can limit per-tenant concurrency, reserve GPU slices, and enforce burst credit system. also can prioritize traffic by token cost. we'll include suggested autoscaler policy in the benchmark doc.
[05:10] Priya S (ML): how do you measure token accounting in the benchmark?
[05:14] Priya (SE): we log token breakouts per-request, cost per token and p99 latency per model variant. the benchmark run will produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and effective cost per 1M tokens.
[05:30] Marcus: can you show a concrete config example?
[05:33] Priya (SE): yes - example: reserved: 2 x a100-eq (base), kept-warm burst: 1 x a100-eq, on-demand burst cap: 2 x a100-eq, fallback: 7B-quantized model pinned to reserved 1 small GPU. autoscaler: scale up threshold at 70% GPU util, scale down after 120s idle, prefer route to fallback after 3 consecutive p99 breaches in 60s.
[06:00] Ethan: what about multi-region fallback? if APAC region is down, route to EU?
[06:04] Priya (SE): yes, smart routing by region and cost is supported. but latency will increase; that's a last-resort fallback.
[06:12] Jordan: we'll put all of this into the POC plan doc and the pricing workbook.
[06:18] Marcus: anything we should be aware of with quantization on your runtime? we need fidelity checks.
[06:22] Priya (SE): we'll run quality regressions against your evaluation prompts and open-source baselines; include automatic eval harness. if accuracy delta > configured threshold we'll flag and recommend different quant profile.
[06:35] Tanya: operations question: audit logs and token-level billing export - do you provide them?
[06:39] Jordan: yes, per-route token and cost export, plus audit logs for Private. will share example CSVs.
[06:46] Marcus: ok good. Let's confirm next steps and owners.
[06:50] Jordan: recap: Jordan send pricing + security pack by 2025-08-25, Priya run benchmark plan starting 2025-08-27, Avalon shares traces by 2025-08-23. follow up call after benchmark. any other Qs?
[07:05] Marcus: none. thanks.
